_comment: A foot block's combat re-face against cavalry inside its ranks keeps the men in their places. A 60-man Infantry block (10 files by 6 ranks) stands on Hold facing north, and a brittle 14-horse Cavalry troop (morale 3) charges it from the north-east. The riders push into the block, so the bearing from the block's anchor to their centre is taken from inside its own footprint and names no front. On main ac16177f each tick's small re-face (under the 75-degree snap threshold) turns the whole slot grid about the anchor with the heading: the men chasing their slots drag the anchor, the bearing moves on, and the grid winds round from -90 to -165.7 degrees, 180 degrees of grid turn in all between ticks 360 and 640 (worst 38.6 degrees in 10 ticks). At ticks 420, 520 and 580 four, six and three men have their slots across the block's centreline from them, and at tick 440 the anchor stands at 893.8, 842.5. Now each such re-face is folded into the formation: the heading still turns onto the riders (to -163 degrees), but the slot grid stays at -90 degrees at every 2-tick sample, so no slot crosses the centreline and the anchor has not been dragged off its ground at tick 440 (900.6, 840.0). The fold stays until the block's next order squares it once the block is clear of the fight. The riders' own re-faces are unchanged: a troop of horse keeps its front to follow. Static camera. Deterministic (scenario + seed + scripted input). Measured with full state dumps every 2 ticks from 360 to 640 on main ac16177f and on the #1792 change (Windows). The first three expects below (tick-8 position, tick-360 Hold, tick-400 FIGHTING) only check the setup and pass on both. The other four are the claims: on the clip seed and perturbed seeds 1 to 4 (SPARTA_DEMO_SEED_RUN) main fails all four on every seed (slots across the centreline 1 to 4 at tick 420, 4 to 6 at 520, 2 to 5 at 580, the anchor 5.4 to 6.9 wu off in x at tick 440), and the change passes all four on every seed. The tick-440 position claim is measured against the spawn point (900, 840); the change's anchor stood at most 1.3 wu off in x and 2.3 in y there, hence the 3.5 wu tolerance.
